guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 authorization-code access for building apps used by others, and the default read scope is documented as read access for the user's account. Per-customer OAuth fits the audience, and the read-only request maps to the default read scope. Setup requires creating an OAuth2 application with redirect URIs and a client secret, then completing code exchange and refresh-token handling. Distribution to other customer workspaces points to submission to Linear's integration directory, but no review duration is quoted in the supplied passages. Setup and execution remain untested.

findings.title: Use the documented OAuth2 authorization-code flow for each customer account
findings.detail: Linear documents OAuth2 as recommended for applications that integrate with Linear, and the authorize endpoint accepts a scope parameter. The default actor is the user who authorized the app, which matches per-customer account access. Tokens are issued to the authorizing user, and the access token is valid for 24 hours.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own Linear account through the OAuth flow.

evidence.quote: Linear supports OAuth2 authentication, which is recommended if you’re building applications to integrate with Linear.
When authorizing a user to the Linear API, redirect to an authorization URL with correct parameters and scopes:
* `user` - (Default) Resources are created as the user who authorized the application. This option should be used if you want each user to do their own authentication

findings.title: Request the read scope for reading issue titles
findings.detail: The read scope is documented as read access for the user's account and is always present by default. The GraphQL example queries issues with id and title fields, and the pagination guide documents first and after cursor arguments for reading beyond the first page. The documented scope boundary is read access for the user's account, not limited to titles, so the app must restrict its queries to issue titles.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads issue titles only and does not create, update or delete issues.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Boundary check: use the individual customer's OAuth access token as Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>, and inspect the actual granted scope and outgoing request log rather than claiming a narrower grant. Send a read-only POST to https://api.linear.app/graphql with query issues(first: 50) selecting nodes id and title plus pageInfo hasNextPage and endCursor. The request must contain no mutation and no create, update, or delete. Expected output: data.issues.nodes with id and title values, and pageInfo showing whether another page exists. This is only the first page; continuation is handled by read-next-issue-titles-page using pageInfo.endCursor while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns data.issues.nodes with title values and a pageInfo object containing hasNextPage and endCursor, and the request log shows only a query.

evidence.quote: --data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \
} ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
``` Or pass the token as an authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`

request.example: curl '-sS' '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 50) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: <ACCESS_TOKEN>: access_token from the token exchange response for the test account

steps.title: Verify the read-only boundary by inspection
steps.detail: Confirm that the token response scope is read and that no write scope such as issues:create or write was requested. The read scope grants read access to the account, so restricting the app to titles is enforced by the app's queries, not by the grant. No mutation is executed.
steps.doneWhen: The token scope and request log show only read queries for id and title, and no issueCreate or issueUpdate operations.

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles with the returned cursor
steps.detail: Pagination: repeat the same read-only query with first: 50 and after set to the pageInfo.endCursor from the prior response, continuing only while the prior response has pageInfo.hasNextPage true. Stop when hasNextPage is false, which is the documented end of the collection; do not treat two pages as a complete listing. Boundary check: use the same individual customer's OAuth token under the default read scope, select only id and title, and confirm in the outgoing request log that no mutation was sent. Do not test any write, create, update, or delete. Expected output: additional issue titles and an updated endCursor.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are fetched until a response returns pageInfo.hasNextPage false, which is the documented end, and the final response has no further cursor to request; the request log shows only queries.

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: read: Candidate only. The read scope and documented first/after cursor pagination support reading issue titles, but setupSteps is empty; the first resource test needs documented OAuth app registration, redirect URI configuration, an authorize request with scope=read, and the code-to-token exchange at https://api.linear.app/oauth/token to obtain the <ACCESS_TOKEN> the requests use.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Create the Linear OAuth2 application and redirect callback
In Linear settings under API, create a new OAuth2 application and configure the redirect callback URL for your test app. Linear recommends a dedicated workspace for managing it because each admin user gets access. Expected successful output: a client ID and client secret for the application. No consent or token is obtained in this step.
Fields: Client ID from the OAuth2 application settings, Client secret from the OAuth2 application settings, Redirect callback URL configured for the test app

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Authorize one test account through the documented OAuth flow
Done when: The redirect returns an authorization code and a matching state value for one test account.

Exchange the authorization code for the test account token
Done when: The token response includes an access_token, refresh_token, and scope value for the test account.

Read the first page of issue titles
Done when: The response returns data.issues.nodes with title values and a pageInfo object containing hasNextPage and endCursor, and the request log shows only a query.

Verify the read-only boundary by inspection
Done when: The token scope and request log show only read queries for id and title, and no issueCreate or issueUpdate operations.

Read the next page of issue titles with the returned cursor
Done when: Pages are fetched until a response returns pageInfo.hasNextPage false, which is the documented end, and the final response has no further cursor to request; the request log shows only queries.
